findings.title: Every removal invalidates the whole mining chunk index, so eviction re-sorts it once per evicted chunk
findings.core_does: m_main_chunkindex is a std::set<ChunkData, ChunkOrder> maintained INCREMENTALLY: ClearChunkData extracts one node when a chunk changes (txgraph.cpp:881-889) and CreateChunkData re-inserts it (txgraph.cpp:892), so a removal costs O(log n) per affected chunk and GetWorstMainChunk (txgraph.cpp:3258) reads m_main_chunkindex.rbegin() with no rebuild. TrimToSize (txmempool.cpp:861-911) can therefore loop GetWorstMainChunk/removeUnchecked at O(log n) per evicted chunk.
findings.we_do: TXGRAPH has no incremental index at all: CHUNK-INDEX is a cached simple-vector that %CLUSTER-UPDATED (txgraph.lisp:281) and TXGRAPH-REMOVE-TRANSACTION (txgraph.lisp:388) set to NIL on ANY mutation, and %ENSURE-CHUNK-INDEX (txgraph.lisp:310) rebuilds it by walking every cluster in the graph, collecting every chunk and SORTing them with %COMPARE-MAIN. MEMPOOL-TRIM-TO-SIZE (mempool.lisp:1726) alternates TXGRAPH-GET-WORST-MAIN-CHUNK with MEMPOOL-REMOVE, so each evicted chunk pays one full O(C log C) rebuild over the WHOLE mempool. MAKE-BLOCK-BUILDER (txgraph.lisp:844) pays one too, so any getblocktemplate or getmempoolfeeratediagram that follows a mempool mutation -- in practice every one of them -- re-sorts the pool.
findings.impact: Measured in the project container on a TXGRAPH of independent transactions: one cached TXGRAPH-GET-WORST-MAIN-CHUNK is ~0 s, but each eviction costs 0.012 s at 20,000 tx, 0.097 s at 100,000 tx and 0.187 s at 200,000 tx (10 evictions took 1.875 s on an idle container, i.e. exactly 10 x the 0.211 s first-index build). Confirmed end to end through the real mempool: with a 30,000-transaction pool, MEMPOOL-TRIM-TO-SIZE evicting 10 transactions took 0.206 s, 0.021 s per transaction -- the same figure the txgraph-level probe gives at that size. A minimal 95-vB entry models 384 bytes of dynamic usage, so the DEFAULT -maxmempool of 300 MB holds several hundred thousand entries (781,250 at that size). MEMPOOL-TRIM-TO-SIZE runs inside MEMPOOL-ADD (mempool.lisp:1018-1022) and HANDLE-TX holds WITH-CURRENT-NODE-LOCK across it (networking/protocol.lisp:1839), so once the pool is at its cap EVERY accepted transaction stalls the entire node -- P2P, block connection and RPC -- for a few tenths of a second, and a block-driven or large-tx trim that evicts k chunks pays k rebuilds. Filling the mempool costs an attacker one round of relay fees; after that every further relayed transaction is amplified into an O(n log n) global sort. Peer-triggerable superlinear blowup.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval of a probe building N singleton transactions in a TXGRAPH then looping TXGRAPH-GET-WORST-MAIN-CHUNK + TXGRAPH-REMOVE-TRANSACTION. Results: (:TXS 20000 :FIRST-INDEX-SECS 0.013 :CACHED-LOOKUP-SECS 0.0 :SECS-PER-EVICTION 0.0120), (:TXS 50000 ... 0.0323), (:TXS 100000 :FIRST-INDEX-SECS 0.106 ... 0.0973), (:TXS 200000 :FIRST-INDEX-SECS 0.211 :SECS-PER-EVICTION 0.1875 on an idle container). Real-mempool probe with *TXGRAPH-SHADOW-CHECKS* bound to NIL: (:POOL-TXS 30000 :USAGE 20640016 :USAGE-PER-TX 688 :REMOVED 10 :TRIM-SECS 0.206 :SECS-PER-REMOVED-TX 0.0206). Modeled usage probe returned (:ENTRY-USAGE 384 :ENTRY-VSIZE 95 :DEFAULT-MAX-SIZE 300000000 :ENTRIES-AT-CAP 781250).

findings.title: RBF staging rebuilds every affected cluster edge by edge, relinearizing once per dependency
findings.core_does: Staging is copy-on-write. PullIn (txgraph.cpp:1693) makes the cluster ACCEPTABLE and then CopyToStaging copies the Cluster object wholesale -- its DepGraph, mapping and linearization come across intact -- so a staged cluster is relinearized at most once, under the ACCEPTABLE_COST budget. GetMainStagingDiagrams (txgraph.cpp:2809) then just walks AppendChunkFeerates over the conflicting main clusters and the staging clusters. rbf.cpp:64-68 states the intent: the 100-cluster rule-5 cap is what bounds 'how many mempool clusters might need to be re-sorted in order to process the replacement'.
findings.we_do: %RBF-STAGED-DIAGRAMS (txgraph.lisp:726) takes the plan's scratch-copy simplification literally: it re-adds every surviving transaction of every affected cluster into a fresh TXGRAPH one at a time, then replays %CLUSTER-REDUCED-EDGES one edge at a time through TXGRAPH-ADD-DEPENDENCY. Each cross-cluster TXGRAPH-ADD-DEPENDENCY (txgraph.lisp:503) pushes onto PENDING-DEPS and calls %RESOLVE-PENDING, which runs %MERGE-GROUP -- rebuilding the merged cluster's depgraph from scratch and re-adding every reduced-parent edge -- and then %CLUSTER-UPDATED, a full SFL relinearization. Reconstructing one k-transaction cluster therefore costs k merges and k relinearizations of growing clusters instead of one memberwise copy.
findings.impact: Measured 0.389-0.396 s for a single TXGRAPH-RBF-DIAGRAMS call at exactly the rule-5 maximum shape (100 clusters x 64 transactions, replacement conflicting with each cluster's tail so 63 of 64 survive and must be rebuilt); 0.084 s at 20 clusters, i.e. linear in cluster count and quadratic in cluster size. CHECK-RBF-RULES runs BEFORE the policy and consensus script passes (validation/transaction.lisp:1218-1256, matching Core's order), and HANDLE-TX holds the node lock across the whole of it (networking/protocol.lisp:1839), so a ~200-byte tx message with a deliberately invalid signature freezes the node for ~0.4 s and is never admitted, never relayed and never pays a fee -- repeatable at zero marginal cost once the attacker has planted the clusters (rules 3/4 gate only on the DECLARED fee, and the transaction is discarded before scripts run). The setup cost (about 6,400 planted mempool transactions and enough coin value to declare the fee) is what keeps this out of S1.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval of a probe building 100 chains of 64 transactions in a TXGRAPH and timing TXGRAPH-RBF-DIAGRAMS with the 100 chain tails as removed handles: (:CLUSTERS 100 :CLUSTER-SIZE 64 :TXS-IN-GRAPH 6400 :REMOVED 100 :OLD-DIAGRAM-CHUNKS 478 :NEW-DIAGRAM-CHUNKS 480 :STAGING-SECS 0.389 on an idle container, 0.396 under load). Same probe at 20 clusters: 0.084 s. The all-removed variant (nothing to rebuild) is 0.001 s, confirming the cost is the survivor reconstruction, not the diagram.

findings.title: prioritisetransaction with an out-of-int64 fee_delta leaves the mempool entry and the txgraph permanently disagreeing
findings.core_does: prioritisetransaction reads the delta as CAmount nAmount = request.params[2].getInt<int64_t>() (rpc/mining.cpp:526). UniValue::getInt<int64_t> range-checks and throws before any state is touched, so an out-of-range fee_delta is a clean JSON-RPC error and the mempool is untouched.
findings.we_do: The handler (rpc/mining.lisp:1018) only checks INTEGERP, and yason parses a JSON integer literal of any magnitude into a bignum. MEMPOOL-PRIORITISE (mempool.lisp:266-272) then does (INCF (MEMPOOL-ENTRY-MODIFIED-FEE ENTRY) FEE-DELTA) FIRST and only afterwards calls TXGRAPH-SET-TRANSACTION-FEE, whose (SETF (FEEFRAC-FEE ...)) hits the (SIGNED-BYTE 64) slot declaration in feefrac.lisp:22 and signals a raw SIMPLE-TYPE-ERROR. The DEFVAR MEMPOOL-DELTAS update and %MEMPOOL-GRAPH-VERIFY are both after the failing call, so neither runs. The same shape is reachable with an in-range delta whose SUM with the existing modified fee overflows int64.
findings.impact: The call raises a TYPE-ERROR out of the RPC layer instead of an RPC error, and leaves the node permanently inconsistent: the mempool entry's modified fee is the bignum while the txgraph -- which is authoritative for mining selection, chunk eviction and the RBF diagram since P4-P6 -- still holds the old fee, and MEMPOOL-DELTAS has no record, so getprioritisedtransactions reports nothing and a mempool.dat round-trip silently drops it. Downstream, %RBF-REPLACED-FEES reads the entry's modified fee, so rule 3 now demands ~1.18e21 satoshis and the transaction becomes unreplaceable; every later prioritisetransaction on the same entry re-raises the same TYPE-ERROR. Operator-triggered (RPC), not remote.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval: (1) TXGRAPH-SET-TRANSACTION-FEE with (expt 2 70) returns (:ERROR TYPE-ERROR "The value 1180591620717411303424 is not of type (SIGNED-BYTE 64) when setting slot FEE of structure FEEFRAC"); (2) (yason:parse "[\"aa\", 0, 1180591620717411303424]") yields the bignum, so the RPC path reaches it; (3) a real mempool with one entry, after MEMPOOL-PRIORITISE with (expt 2 70), reports (:ERROR (TYPE-ERROR) :ENTRY-MODIFIED-FEE-BEFORE 10000 :ENTRY-MODIFIED-FEE-AFTER 1180591620717411313424 :GRAPH-FEE-BEFORE 10000 :GRAPH-FEE-AFTER 10000 :DELTAS-COUNT 0).

findings.title: txgraph sizes are sigop-adjusted vbytes where Core uses sigop-adjusted weight
findings.core_does: Core's TxGraph works entirely in WEIGHT units: StageAddition builds FeePerWeight(fee, GetSigOpsAdjustedWeight(GetTransactionWeight(tx), sigops_cost, nBytesPerSigOp)) (txmempool.cpp:1017) and MakeTxGraph is given max_cluster_size = limits.cluster_size_vbytes * WITNESS_SCALE_FACTOR = 404,000 WU (txmempool.cpp:181). Chunk feerates, ChunkLinearization's absorb test, CompareMainTransactions and the cluster size limit are all fee-per-weight; the division by 4 happens only at the consumer boundary via ToFeePerVSize (policy.h:196).
findings.we_do: MEMPOOL-ADD passes (MEMPOOL-ENTRY-VSIZE ENTRY) = SIGOP-ADJUSTED-VSIZE = ceil(max(weight, sigops*20)/4) (mempool.lisp:130-138, 968), and +MAX-CLUSTER-SIZE+ is 101,000 vB (txgraph.lisp:49). The per-transaction ceiling is applied BEFORE the cross-multiplied feerate comparisons rather than after, so two transactions whose weights differ by 1-3 WU become indistinguishable to FEEFRAC>> and FEERATE-COMPARE.
findings.impact: Chunk BOUNDARIES, not just tie order, can differ from Core. Executed: a 2-transaction cluster with parent (fee 100, weight 404) and child (fee 100, weight 401) is ONE chunk (200, 805) in Core -- the child's feerate is strictly higher, so it absorbs the parent -- and TWO chunks ((100,101),(100,101)) for us, so eviction drops the child alone where Core drops the CPFP pair, and the rolling-minimum-fee bump differs. Mining order can strictly flip: singleton clusters X(fee 101, weight 401) and Y(fee 100, weight 397) have Y strictly ahead of X in Core, while our cross product is exactly 0 so the order is decided by the txid fallback. The cluster size limit is also up to 0.75 vB per transaction stricter than Core's 404,000 WU (~48 vB on a 64-transaction cluster). All three effects are bounded by the sub-1% rounding, and the unit choice is documented in assembler.lisp:258-266 and rpc/mempool.lisp:289 -- but those docstrings record only the RPC unit and claim the ordering matches Core 'up to the per-tx ceiling', which the chunk-boundary and strict-flip cases show is not so.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval of a probe running our chunker on the vsize graph and computing Core's weight-based verdict side by side: (:CORE-CHILD-ABSORBS-PARENT T :OURS-CHILD-ABSORBS-PARENT NIL :OUR-CHUNK-COUNT 2 :OUR-CHUNKS ((100 . 101) (100 . 101)) :CORE-WOULD-BE-CHUNKS ((200 . 805)) :ORDER-FLIP (:CORE-MINES-Y-FIRST T :OUR-CROSS-PRODUCT 0 :OUR-VERDICT :TIE-BROKEN-BY-TXID)).

findings.title: RBF descendant expansion runs before the rule-5 cluster cap meant to bound it
findings.core_does: GetEntriesForConflicts checks the rule-5 cluster cap FIRST and returns the error before touching descendants; only then does it loop CalculateDescendants over iters_conflicting. The comment at rbf.cpp:78-79 is explicit about why: 'The cluster count limit ensures that we won't do too much work on a single invocation of this function.'
findings.we_do: CHECK-RBF-RULES binds (REPLACED (%RBF-REPLACED-SET MEMPOOL DIRECT-CONFLICTS)) in the LET at mempool.lisp:1245-1246, so the full descendant expansion over every direct conflict runs unconditionally, and %RBF-CLUSTER-CAPS is only consulted in the body afterwards. The number of direct conflicts is bounded only by the candidate's input count (~1,400-2,400 for a maximum-standard-weight transaction), not by the 100-cluster cap.
findings.impact: Wasted work on a replacement that rule 5 is about to reject, and the work is peer-supplied: each direct conflict drags in up to its whole 64-transaction cluster. Measured 0.009 s of descendant expansion for 200 conflicts spanning 12,800 mempool transactions before the cap returned :TOO-MANY-CLUSTERS (the cap check itself was below timer resolution). Extrapolating to a maximum-input transaction against fully populated clusters puts it around 0.1 s per rejected message under the node lock. Bounded divergence, and the ceiling is low enough that it is a hygiene fix rather than a DoS on its own -- but it removes the guarantee Core's ordering exists to provide.
findings.executed: scripts/dev.sh eval of a probe building 200 mempool chains of 64 transactions and timing %RBF-REPLACED-SET and %RBF-CLUSTER-CAPS separately over the 200 chain roots: (:MEMPOOL-TXS 12800 :DIRECT-CONFLICTS 200 :REPLACED-SET-SIZE 12800 :DESCENDANT-EXPANSION-SECS 0.009 :CLUSTER-CAP-SECS 0.0 :CAP-VERDICT :TOO-MANY-CLUSTERS).

coverage_note: Read both trees for feefrac.lisp vs util/feefrac.{h,cpp}, cluster-linearize.lisp vs cluster_linearize.h (DepGraph, chunking, PostLinearize), spanning-forest.lisp vs the SFL SpanningForestState and Linearize, txgraph.lisp vs txgraph.{h,cpp} (cluster registry, Updated/CompareMainTransactions, block builder, GetWorstMainChunk, Trim, staging diagrams), the mempool.lisp consumers (add/remove/trim/GetMinFee/RBF/package limits/reorg bulk re-add) vs txmempool.cpp and validation.cpp ReplacementChecks + PackageRBFChecks, and assembler.lisp vs node/miner.cpp addChunks. Executed in the project container throughout (probes driven through scripts/dev.sh eval). The pure algorithm layer came back clean line for line: CompareChunks including the done_0/done_1 side selection and the equal-size B-advance, EvaluateFee rounding, DepGraph RemoveTransactions/AddDependencies/GetReducedParents snapshot semantics, PostLinearize's merge/swap and both output directions, and the whole SFL port (Activate/Deactivate/MergeChunks/PickMergeCandidate/PickChunkToOptimize/PickDependencyToSplit/MinimizeStep/GetLinearization and the cost-model coefficients) all match Core; Trim matches Core's heap-plus-union-find shape including the not-included-implies-descendants-removed property; GetMinFee matches txmempool.cpp:829-851 exactly. NOT REPORTED, checked and found equivalent: the spends-conflicting-tx test (our direct-input-vs-replaced-set form is equivalent to Core's ancestors-vs-direct-conflicts form because the replaced set is descendant-closed), the package-RBF exact feerate comparison (CFeeRate really does delegate to FeeRateCompare at d3056bc, so the earlier truncation fix is right), rule 5's cluster counting, and the block builder's Skip semantics (our unconditional cluster exclusion is a memory, not a behaviour, difference from Core's m_known_end_of_cluster). MEASURED AND JUDGED BENIGN: LINEARIZE runs with no cost budget where Core caps each relinearization at ACCEPTABLE_COST 75,000 (POST_CHANGE_COST 375,000 in background DoWork); a 400-shape random search over 64-transaction clusters found a worst SFL cost of 102,741 -- above Core's budget -- but the wall time never exceeded 0.35 ms per LINEARIZE, and the divergence is documented in the LINEARIZE docstring. Also measured: a rejected over-limit MEMPOOL-ADD rolls the txgraph back byte-identically (two chains of 40 and 30, a joining transaction that trips IS-OVERSIZED, then removal: cluster membership, linearization order and every chunk feerate come back identical and TXGRAPH-SANITY-CHECK passes), so the fact that our reject path mutates the MAIN graph where Core stages in a separate level costs nothing observable. Also measured: LINEARIZE's output and its chunk feerate multiset are seed-independent over 200 random 12-transaction clusters x 8 seeds, so the fresh per-call RNG seed does not make mining order or the RBF diagram nondeterministic. NOT COVERED: (a) the fee estimator and block-policy estimator (src/mempool/fee-estimator.lisp, block-policy-estimator.lisp) -- they share the directory but not the cluster machinery; they belong to GA11 dimension 8 (rpc/util + fees + versionbits); (b) the orphan pool (src/mempool/orphan.lisp) and everything about which transaction is requested and when -- GA11 dimension 4 (transaction relay scheduling); (c) TRUC/BIP431 topology rules and the 1p1c package assembly path beyond their txgraph calls -- mempool-policy; (d) the getmempoolentry / getmempoolcluster / getmempoolfeeratediagram JSON shapes and field names (their unit divergence from Core is documented in the handlers) -- GA11 dimension 8; (e) mempool.dat persistence -- untouched by cluster mempool by design; (f) no long-running soak or concurrent-thread test was run, so a race between the block-builder observer count and a mutating thread is unexamined -- the assembler takes the node lock, but nothing was executed to prove no path reaches MAKE-BLOCK-BUILDER without it.
